question_record.context: In the investigation of a security incident involving active unknown malware that was detected on a machine, it was identified that a user account might have been compromised and used to drop ransomware-related files on several devices. This could potentially be part of an attack aiming at lateral movement across the network.
question_record.question: During a potential lateral movement, an IP address is associated with another device. Can you provide the IP address that was related to the possible lateral movement attempt?
solution: There is a detection of active unknown malware on the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
There was lateral movement to the jump server from IP address `99.83.111.100` using PSExec.
There is a possible compromised user account delivering ransomware-related files on host `vnevado-win11u`.
Possible lateral movement was observed from IP address `38.142.109.10`.

150.name: Active unknown malware was detected
150.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.

174.name: PSExec to Vnevado-jump
174.description: Lateral movement to the jump server

41.name: Possible compromised user account delivering ransomware-related files
41.description: A user account was observed dropping a ransomware-related file on several devices. An attacker may have compromised the said user account to move laterally across the network and infect as many devices with ransomware as possible. Automated remediation action may be taken to disable the account.

101.name: Possible lateral movement
101.description: Lateral movement on another device was observed in close time proximity to a suspicious network event on this device. This could mean that an attacker is attempting to move laterally across devices to gather data or elevate privileges. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint alert.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Command_File_Mention' AND o.Concept = 'Device_AAD_ID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s,%s,%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501

SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Device_AAD_ID' AND o.Concept = 'IP_Address'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501

SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'IP_Address' AND o.Concept = 'Host_Name'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s,%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
